40	class AuditedMCPServer(MCPServer[AppContext]):
41	    """An MCPServer that records an audit event for every tool call."""

43	    rate_limiter: RateLimiter
44	    mcpg_settings: Settings
45	    in_flight_calls: int = 0
46	    # OpenTelemetry tracer. ``None`` when MCPG_OTEL_ENABLED=false or
47	    # the ``mcpg[otel]`` extra isn't installed — :func:`tool_span`
48	    # treats both cases as no-ops so ``call_tool`` doesn't branch.
49	    otel_tracer: TracerHandle | None = None
50	
51	    def _log_if_slow(self, name: str, duration: float) -> None:
52	        if not hasattr(self, "mcpg_settings"):
53	            return
54	        threshold_ms = self.mcpg_settings.slow_call_threshold_ms
55	        if threshold_ms <= 0:
56	            return
57	        threshold_sec = threshold_ms / 1000.0
58	        if duration > threshold_sec:
59	            import logging
60	
61	            logger = logging.getLogger("mcpg.server")
62	            logger.warning(
63	                "Slow tool call: %s took %.3fs (threshold: %.3fs)",
64	                name,
65	                duration,
66	                threshold_sec,
67	            )

69	    async def call_tool(
70	        self, name: str, arguments: dict[str, Any], context: Context[AppContext, Any] | None = None
71	    ) -> CallToolResult | InputRequiredResult:
72	        self.in_flight_calls += 1
73	        try:
74	            # Enforce rate limiting if configured
75	            if hasattr(self, "rate_limiter"):
76	                allowed = await self.rate_limiter.consume(name)
77	                if not allowed:
78	                    raise RuntimeError(f"Rate limit exceeded for tool {name!r}. Please try again later.")
79	
80	            metrics = get_metrics()
81	            # Resolve the capability bucket once per call so both the
82	            # OTel span attribute and the Prometheus counter carry the
83	            # same label. `classify_tool` returns None for tools that
84	            # don't match any override / pattern — defensively use
85	            # "unknown" so the label dimension stays cardinality-stable.
86	            bucket = about.classify_tool(name) or "unknown"
87	            start = time.monotonic()
88	            try:
89	                with tool_span(self.otel_tracer, name, arguments, bucket=bucket):
90	                    result = await super().call_tool(name, arguments, context)
91	            except Exception as exc:
92	                duration = time.monotonic() - start
93	                self._log_if_slow(name, duration)
94	                audit.record(audit.AuditEvent(tool=name, arguments=arguments, status="error", error=str(exc)))
95	                metrics.record_call(name, "error", duration, bucket=bucket)
96	                raise
97	            duration = time.monotonic() - start
98	            self._log_if_slow(name, duration)
99	            audit.record(audit.AuditEvent(tool=name, arguments=arguments, status="ok"))
100	            metrics.record_call(name, "ok", duration, bucket=bucket)

102	        finally:

107	    settings: Settings,
108	    database: Database,
109	    listen_manager: ListenManager,
110	    cursor_manager: CursorManager,
111	    analytical_runner: AnalyticalRunner | None = None,
112	) -> Callable[[MCPServer[AppContext]], AbstractAsyncContextManager[AppContext]]:
113	    """Build the server lifespan: open the database on start, close on stop.
114	
115	    The listen manager is created eagerly (cheap — it doesn't open the
116	    listener connection until the first ``subscribe_channel`` call) and
117	    torn down on lifespan exit so subscriptions can't outlive the
118	    server. The cursor manager holds dedicated connections per open
119	    server-side cursor and is closed-out symmetrically.
120	    """
121	
122	    @asynccontextmanager
123	    async def lifespan(_server: MCPServer[AppContext]) -> AsyncIterator[AppContext]:
124	        from mcpg.cache import CacheManager, cache_namespace
125	
126	        cache_manager = CacheManager(
127	            enabled=settings.cache_enabled,
128	            ttl_seconds=settings.cache_ttl_seconds,
129	            maxsize=settings.cache_maxsize,
130	            redis_url=settings.redis_url,
131	            namespace=cache_namespace(settings.database_url),
132	        )
133	        await cache_manager.start()
134	        if analytical_runner is not None:
135	            await analytical_runner.start()
136	        try:
137	            async with database, listen_manager, cursor_manager:
138	                yield AppContext(
139	                    settings=settings,
140	                    database=database,
141	                    listen_manager=listen_manager,
142	                    cursor_manager=cursor_manager,
143	                    cache=cache_manager,
144	                    analytical_runner=analytical_runner,
145	                )
146	        finally:
147	            if analytical_runner is not None:
148	                await analytical_runner.close()
149	            if hasattr(_server, "in_flight_calls"):
150	                import asyncio
151	                import logging
152	
153	                logger = logging.getLogger("mcpg.server")
154	
155	                drain_start = time.monotonic()
156	                drain_timeout = settings.shutdown_drain_seconds
157	
158	                while _server.in_flight_calls > 0:
159	                    elapsed = time.monotonic() - drain_start
160	                    if elapsed >= drain_timeout:
161	                        logger.warning(
162	                            "Shutdown drain timed out after %ds; force exiting with %d tool calls in-flight",
163	                            drain_timeout,
164	                            _server.in_flight_calls,
165	                        )
166	                        break
167	                    logger.info("Waiting for %d in-flight tool calls to drain...", _server.in_flight_calls)
168	                    await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
169	
170	            await cache_manager.close()
171	
172	            # Flush pending OTel spans so a clean shutdown doesn't
173	            # drop the last batch of traces. Tracer is process-wide
174	            # global but the provider hung off the server lets us
175	            # invoke shutdown only when we actually own it.
176	            if hasattr(_server, "otel_tracer") and _server.otel_tracer is not None:
177	                _server.otel_tracer.shutdown()
178

194	        database: Optional pre-built database (used by tests); otherwise one
195	            is created from ``settings``.
196	        listen_manager: Optional pre-built listen manager (used by tests

210	    lm = (

80	    constant-time — a tiny precaution against timing oracles, but a
81	    free one given how easy it is to write.
82	    """

84	    def __init__(self, app: object, *, token: str, exempt_paths: frozenset[str] = _AUTH_EXEMPT_PATHS) -> None:
85	        self._app = app
86	        self._token = token
87	        self._exempt = exempt_paths

89	    async def __call__(self, scope: dict[str, object], receive: object, send: object) -> None:
90	        if scope["type"] != "http":
91	            # Non-HTTP scopes (lifespan) pass straight through; the auth
92	            # gate only makes sense for actual requests.
93	            await self._app(scope, receive, send)  # type: ignore[operator]
94	            return
95	
96	        path = str(scope.get("path", ""))
97	        if path in self._exempt:
98	            await self._app(scope, receive, send)  # type: ignore[operator]
99	            return
100	
101	        headers: list[tuple[bytes, bytes]] = scope.get("headers", [])  # type: ignore[assignment]
102	        auth_header = b""
103	        for key, value in headers:
104	            if key.lower() == b"authorization":
105	                auth_header = value
106	                break
107	
108	        if not auth_header.startswith(b"Bearer "):
109	            await _send_401(send, "missing Authorization: Bearer header")
110	            return
111	
112	        presented = auth_header[len(b"Bearer ") :].decode("utf-8", errors="ignore").strip()
113	        if not hmac.compare_digest(presented, self._token):

120	class _OIDCAuthMiddleware:
121	    """ASGI middleware that validates the bearer JWT against an OIDC issuer.
122	
123	    When ``role_claim`` is configured AND the JWT carries that claim,
124	    the claim's value is also stashed in
125	    :data:`mcpg.tenancy.current_role` so the tenanted driver issues
126	    ``SET LOCAL ROLE`` for the request. This replaces the
127	    ``X-MCPG-Role`` header path for OIDC deployments — the issuer
128	    becomes the single source of truth for which role the caller can
129	    assume.
130	    """
131	
132	    def __init__(
133	        self,
134	        app: object,
135	        *,
136	        verifier: OIDCVerifier,
137	        exempt_paths: frozenset[str] = _AUTH_EXEMPT_PATHS,
138	    ) -> None:
139	        self._app = app
140	        self._verifier = verifier
141	        self._exempt = exempt_paths
142	
143	    async def __call__(self, scope: dict[str, object], receive: object, send: object) -> None:
144	        if scope["type"] != "http":
145	            await self._app(scope, receive, send)  # type: ignore[operator]
146	            return
147	
148	        path = str(scope.get("path", ""))
149	        if path in self._exempt:
150	            await self._app(scope, receive, send)  # type: ignore[operator]
151	            return
152	
153	        headers: list[tuple[bytes, bytes]] = scope.get("headers", [])  # type: ignore[assignment]
154	        auth_header = b""
155	        for key, value in headers:
156	            if key.lower() == b"authorization":
157	                auth_header = value
158	                break
159	
160	        if not auth_header.startswith(b"Bearer "):
161	            await _send_401(send, "missing Authorization: Bearer header")
162	            return
163	
164	        token = auth_header[len(b"Bearer ") :].decode("utf-8", errors="ignore").strip()
165	        try:
166	            verified = await self._verifier.verify(token)
167	        except OIDCError as exc:
168	            logger.warning("OIDC verification failed: %s", exc)
169	            await _send_401(send, "invalid bearer token")
170	            return
171	
172	        if verified.role is None:
173	            await self._app(scope, receive, send)  # type: ignore[operator]
174	            return
175	
176	        # JWT carried a role claim — validate it as an identifier
177	        # before stashing so an attacker-controlled value can't break
178	        # the SQL the tenancy driver inlines.
179	        try:
180	            validate_role(verified.role)
181	        except TenancyError:
182	            logger.warning("OIDC role claim has unsafe identifier: %r", verified.role)
183	            await _send_401(send, "role claim contains an invalid identifier")
184	            return
185	
186	        # Stash on the scope so the tool-dispatch task (a separate, session-
187	        # scoped task on HTTP/SSE) reads the correct per-request role via the
188	        # SDK request context; the ContextVar alone doesn't reach it.
189	        scope[_ROLE_SCOPE_KEY] = verified.role
190	        reset_token = current_role.set(verified.role)
191	        try:
192	            await self._app(scope, receive, send)  # type: ignore[operator]
193	        finally:
194	            current_role.reset(reset_token)

198	    """ASGI middleware that parses ``X-MCPG-Role`` into a ContextVar.
199	
200	    Per-request multi-tenancy: when the header is present, validate it
201	    against the allowlist (when one is configured) and set
202	    :data:`mcpg.tenancy.current_role`. The
203	    :class:`mcpg.tenancy.TenantSqlDriver` then issues
204	    ``SET LOCAL ROLE`` inside every query's transaction so the role
205	    auto-resets when the transaction ends.
206	
207	    Skips non-HTTP scopes and the same exempt paths as
208	    :class:`_BearerAuthMiddleware` so probes don't try to acquire a
209	    role they don't need.
210	    """
211	
212	    def __init__(
213	        self,
214	        app: object,
215	        *,
216	        allowed_roles: tuple[str, ...] = (),
217	        exempt_paths: frozenset[str] = _AUTH_EXEMPT_PATHS,
218	    ) -> None:
219	        self._app = app
220	        self._allowed = frozenset(allowed_roles)
221	        self._exempt = exempt_paths
222	
223	    async def __call__(self, scope: dict[str, object], receive: object, send: object) -> None:
224	        if scope["type"] != "http":
225	            await self._app(scope, receive, send)  # type: ignore[operator]
226	            return
227	
228	        path = str(scope.get("path", ""))
229	        if path in self._exempt:
230	            await self._app(scope, receive, send)  # type: ignore[operator]
231	            return
232	
233	        headers: list[tuple[bytes, bytes]] = scope.get("headers", [])  # type: ignore[assignment]
234	        role_header: bytes | None = None
235	        for key, value in headers:
236	            if key.lower() == b"x-mcpg-role":
237	                role_header = value
238	                break
239	
240	        if role_header is None:
241	            # No per-request override; the driver will fall back to
242	            # the static default_role from Settings.
243	            await self._app(scope, receive, send)  # type: ignore[operator]
244	            return
245	
246	        role = role_header.decode("utf-8", errors="ignore").strip()
247	        try:
248	            validate_role(role)
249	        except TenancyError:
250	            await _send_403(send, "X-MCPG-Role contains an invalid identifier")
251	            return
252	
253	        if self._allowed and role not in self._allowed:
254	            await _send_403(send, "X-MCPG-Role is not in the allowed-roles list")
255	            return
256	
257	        # Stash on the scope so the tool-dispatch task (a separate, session-
258	        # scoped task on HTTP/SSE) reads the correct per-request role via the
259	        # SDK request context; the ContextVar alone doesn't reach it.
260	        scope[_ROLE_SCOPE_KEY] = role
261	        token = current_role.set(role)
262	        try:
263	            await self._app(scope, receive, send)  # type: ignore[operator]
264	        finally:
265	            current_role.reset(token)

333	class _IPAllowlistMiddleware:
334	    """ASGI middleware that rejects clients whose IP isn't on the allowlist.
335	
336	    The allowlist is a tuple of IP-address or CIDR-range strings. Each
337	    entry is pre-parsed into an ``ipaddress`` network at construction
338	    time so the request-time check is just a membership test.
339	
340	    The matching IP is the **immediate** connecting peer
341	    (``scope["client"][0]``). ``X-Forwarded-For`` is deliberately
342	    *not* honoured: trusting a forwarded header without a verified
343	    upstream is a well-known spoofing vector, and operators behind a
344	    reverse proxy already terminate TLS there and can enforce the
345	    allowlist at that layer (where it composes with the proxy's own
346	    auditing).
347	
348	    Failure mode is a minimal 403 — no header echo, no body specifics
349	    — so a scanning attacker can't fingerprint the allowlist from the
350	    response.
351	    """
352	
353	    def __init__(self, app: object, *, allowlist: tuple[str, ...]) -> None:
354	        import ipaddress
355	
356	        self._app = app
357	        # Pre-parse once at construction. ``strict=False`` makes
358	        # single addresses like ``1.2.3.4`` valid networks (their
359	        # /32 or /128 sibling), so membership testing is uniform
360	        # across single-IP and CIDR entries.
361	        self._networks: tuple[ipaddress.IPv4Network | ipaddress.IPv6Network, ...] = tuple(
362	            ipaddress.ip_network(entry, strict=False) for entry in allowlist
363	        )
364	
365	    async def __call__(self, scope: dict[str, object], receive: object, send: object) -> None:
366	        if scope["type"] != "http":
367	            await self._app(scope, receive, send)  # type: ignore[operator]
368	            return
369	
370	        if not self._client_is_allowed(scope):
371	            await _send_403(send, "ip not on allowlist")
372	            return
373	
374	        await self._app(scope, receive, send)  # type: ignore[operator]
375	
376	    def _client_is_allowed(self, scope: dict[str, object]) -> bool:
377	        import ipaddress
378	
379	        client = scope.get("client")
380	        # ASGI spec says ``client`` is a two-item iterable ``[host, port]``
381	        # — most servers hand it back as a tuple, some hand back a list,
382	        # so accept both. A missing entry can't be matched against any
383	        # allowlist; deny so a bug in a transport layer can't accidentally
384	        # turn the gate off.
385	        if not isinstance(client, (list, tuple)) or not client:
386	            return False
387	        try:
388	            peer = ipaddress.ip_address(str(client[0]))
389	        except ValueError:
390	            return False
391	        return any(peer in network for network in self._networks)

482	class _RequestTimeoutMiddleware:
483	    """ASGI middleware that caps wall-clock time for a single request.
484	
485	    Off by default (``MCPG_HTTP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=0``); only
486	    installed when a positive timeout is configured. Intended for
487	    request/response deployments — note that a hard cap will also cut
488	    off long-lived streaming responses, so leave it disabled if you
489	    rely on long SSE / streamable-http streams.
490	
491	    On expiry, if the downstream app has not started the response yet,
492	    a 504 is emitted; if bytes were already sent we can only abort the
493	    stream (the status line is long gone).
494	    """
495	
496	    def __init__(self, app: object, *, timeout_seconds: int) -> None:
497	        self._app = app
498	        self._timeout = timeout_seconds
499	
500	    async def __call__(self, scope: dict[str, object], receive: object, send: object) -> None:
501	        if scope["type"] != "http":
502	            await self._app(scope, receive, send)  # type: ignore[operator]
503	            return
504	
505	        started = False
506	
507	        async def send_wrapper(message: dict[str, object]) -> None:
508	            nonlocal started
509	            if message["type"] == "http.response.start":
510	                started = True
511	            await send(message)  # type: ignore[operator]
512	
513	        try:
514	            async with asyncio.timeout(self._timeout):
515	                await self._app(scope, receive, send_wrapper)  # type: ignore[operator]
516	        except TimeoutError:
517	            # On Python 3.11+ ``asyncio.TimeoutError`` IS the builtin
518	            # ``TimeoutError`` (the asyncio name is a deprecated alias —
519	            # ruff UP041 rejects it), so they can't be distinguished
520	            # at catch time. If an inner app ever raises a bare
521	            # ``TimeoutError`` we'd mis-attribute it to our cap; this
522	            # is preferable to leaking an exception out of the
523	            # middleware. Inner apps that want to surface their own
524	            # timeout should raise a domain-specific subclass.
525	            # Only safe to write a status line if the app hasn't already.
526	            if not started:
527	                await _send_504(send, f"request exceeded {self._timeout}s")

530	def build_http_app(server: object, settings: Settings, *, kind: str) -> Starlette:
531	    """Wrap an MCPServer HTTP app with metrics + optional auth.
532	
533	    Args:
534	        server: A ``MCPServer`` instance.
535	        settings: Active server settings.
536	        kind: ``"streamable-http"`` or ``"sse"``.
537	
538	    Returns:
539	        A Starlette app with ``/metrics`` mounted and (when
540	        ``settings.http_auth_token`` is set) bearer-token auth on
541	        everything except the exempt paths.
542	    """
543	    from starlette.routing import Route
544	
545	    if kind == "streamable-http":
546	        app = server.streamable_http_app()  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
547	    elif kind == "sse":
548	        app = server.sse_app()  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
549	    else:
550	        raise ValueError(f"unknown HTTP transport kind: {kind!r}")
551	
552	    # Mount /metrics + /healthz on the existing router. Starlette
553	    # exposes the underlying router via .router; appending Route
554	    # objects is the idiomatic way to extend the route table without
555	    # subclassing.
556	    app.router.routes.append(Route("/metrics", _metrics_response_factory(), methods=["GET"]))
557	    app.router.routes.append(Route("/healthz", _health_response_factory(), methods=["GET"]))

559	    # Middleware stack ordering:
560	    #   In OIDC mode, the OIDC middleware verifies the JWT AND stashes
561	    #   the role-claim into current_role itself — so the tenant

563	    #   truth for the role). In static mode, the X-MCPG-Role
564	    #   middleware sits ABOVE the bearer-token middleware so

588	                "bearer tokens on every request.",
589	                kind,
590	            )

592	    # Outer middlewares (processed first on request)
593	    app.add_middleware(_SecurityHeadersMiddleware, hsts_max_age=settings.http_hsts_max_age)
594	    app.add_middleware(_RequestSizeLimitMiddleware, max_bytes=settings.http_max_body_bytes)

597	    if settings.http_request_timeout_seconds > 0:
598	        app.add_middleware(_RequestTimeoutMiddleware, timeout_seconds=settings.http_request_timeout_seconds)

611	    # first per Starlette's middleware stacking) so denied clients
612	    # never reach the auth / size-limit / body-read middlewares — the

618	    # but mypy under strict mode loses the type through the .add_middleware
619	    # call (returns None). Cast through Any to settle the return type
620	    # without hiding real type errors.
621	    from typing import cast as _cast
622	
623	    return _cast("Starlette", app)

626	def run_http(server: object, settings: Settings, *, kind: str) -> None:
627	    """Build the wrapped HTTP app and serve it via uvicorn.
628	
629	    Honours the project's TLS / mTLS settings: when
630	    ``http_tls_certfile`` + ``http_tls_keyfile`` are set, uvicorn
631	    terminates TLS itself. Adding ``http_tls_ca_certs`` and
632	    flipping ``http_tls_client_cert_required=true`` upgrades the
633	    listener to full mutual TLS — connections without a client cert
634	    signed by a CA in the bundle are refused at the handshake
635	    layer, before any ASGI middleware sees the request.
636	    """
637	    import ssl
638	
639	    import uvicorn
640	
641	    app = build_http_app(server, settings, kind=kind)
642	    tls_kwargs = _uvicorn_tls_kwargs(settings, ssl_module=ssl)
643	    # Windows: async psycopg refuses to run on the ProactorEventLoop and
644	    # needs a SelectorEventLoop. ``__main__`` sets the selector policy at
645	    # startup, but uvicorn's own loop setup reinstalls the *proactor*
646	    # policy on Windows before serving — which silently breaks every
647	    # database connection under the HTTP transport (the connection pool
648	    # times out after 30s and the session crashes). stdio is unaffected;
649	    # nothing overrides the policy there. Re-pin the selector policy and
650	    # tell uvicorn to leave the loop alone (``loop="none"``) so it runs on
651	    # the loop our policy creates. No-op off Windows.
652	    if sys.platform == "win32":
653	        # CPython 3.14 privatized WindowsSelectorEventLoopPolicy to
654	        # _WindowsSelectorEventLoopPolicy; fall back to it when the public
655	        # name is gone so this keeps working on 3.12-3.14. Reading the
656	        # removed public name can raise NameError (not AttributeError) via
657	        # asyncio's own deprecation shim, which a bare getattr(..., default)
658	        # would NOT catch — a plain try/except is used instead, and a
659	        # missing private name too fails with the clear RuntimeError below
660	        # rather than an obscure AttributeError/NameError.
661	        try:
662	            # mypy's python_version=3.14 target sheds the public name from
663	            # typeshed entirely (see pyproject.toml's [tool.mypy]) — this is
664	            # exactly the removed-on-3.14 case the except branch below handles
665	            # at runtime; ignore is scoped to this one attribute reference.
666	            selector_policy_cls = asyncio.WindowsSelectorEventLoopPolicy  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
667	        except (AttributeError, NameError):
668	            selector_policy_cls = getattr(asyncio, "_WindowsSelectorEventLoopPolicy", None)
669	        if selector_policy_cls is None:
670	            raise RuntimeError(
671	                "mcpg: this Python's asyncio module exposes neither WindowsSelectorEventLoopPolicy "
672	                "nor _WindowsSelectorEventLoopPolicy; the Windows selector-loop policy mcpg needs for "
673	                "psycopg can't be set. Please file a bug with your Python version."
674	            )
675	        asyncio.set_event_loop_policy(selector_policy_cls())
676	        tls_kwargs["loop"] = "none"
677	    # mypy can't reason about ``**dict[str, object]`` against the
678	    # large, overloaded ``uvicorn.run`` signature; the dict's contents
679	    # are already constrained by ``_uvicorn_tls_kwargs``.
680	    uvicorn.run(app, host=settings.http_host, port=settings.http_port, **tls_kwargs)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
681	
682	
683	def _uvicorn_tls_kwargs(settings: Settings, *, ssl_module: object) -> dict[str, object]:
684	    """Translate the project's TLS settings into the uvicorn keyword arg shape.
685	
686	    ``ssl_module`` is parameterised so tests can pass a stub without
687	    importing the real :mod:`ssl` (avoids creating a real SSL context
688	    just to assert the argument routing). At runtime callers pass
689	    ``ssl`` directly.
690	
691	    Returns an empty dict when TLS isn't configured, so the call site
692	    can ``uvicorn.run(..., **tls_kwargs)`` unconditionally.
693	    """
694	    if settings.http_tls_certfile is None or settings.http_tls_keyfile is None:
695	        return {}
696	    kwargs: dict[str, object] = {
697	        "ssl_certfile": settings.http_tls_certfile,
698	        "ssl_keyfile": settings.http_tls_keyfile,
699	        # Pin to PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER explicitly. On Python 3.10+ this
700	        # carries SSLContext.minimum_version = TLSv1_2 by default, so
701	        # an old system OpenSSL can't silently negotiate TLS 1.0/1.1
702	        # even though uvicorn would otherwise accept whatever its own
703	        # default SSLContext allows. Pinning this here makes the
704	        # version-floor explicit at the call site so a uvicorn upgrade
705	        # can't quietly loosen it.
706	        "ssl_version": ssl_module.PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER,  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
707	        # AEAD-only cipher allowlist matching the Mozilla "intermediate"
708	        # config (https://wiki.mozilla.org/Security/Server_Side_TLS).
709	        # All entries are ECDHE / DHE with AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305
710	        # — no RC4, no 3DES, no CBC modes, no NULL, no anonymous.
711	        # TLS 1.3 suites are negotiated separately and aren't listed
712	        # here (they're enabled unconditionally on a TLS 1.3 handshake).
713	        "ssl_ciphers": _MOZILLA_INTERMEDIATE_CIPHERS,
714	    }
715	    if settings.http_tls_ca_certs is not None:
716	        kwargs["ssl_ca_certs"] = settings.http_tls_ca_certs
717	    if settings.http_tls_client_cert_required:
718	        # ``ssl.CERT_REQUIRED`` tells the TLS handshake to refuse a
719	        # connection whose client cert isn't signed by a CA in the
720	        # configured bundle. config.load_settings already enforces the
721	        # ``ca_certs`` invariant so this combination is always valid.
722	        kwargs["ssl_cert_reqs"] = ssl_module.CERT_REQUIRED  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
723	    return kwargs
724	
725	
726	# Mozilla intermediate cipher suite list (last updated 2024-02 generator
727	# output, AEAD-only). Pinned as a module-level constant so the value is
728	# auditable at one site rather than hidden in the kwargs builder.
729	_MOZILLA_INTERMEDIATE_CIPHERS = ":".join(
730	    [
731	        "ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256",
732	        "ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256",
733	        "ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384",
734	        "ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384",
735	        "ECDHE-ECDSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305",
736	        "ECDHE-RSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305",
737	        "DHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256",
738	        "DHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384",
739	    ]
740	)

62	def _compile_secret_name_pattern(extra: str | None) -> re.Pattern[str]:
63	    patterns = list(_DEFAULT_SECRET_NAME_PATTERNS)

109	def _redact_value(value: Any) -> Any:
110	    """Recursively mask credentials in dicts, lists, tuples, and strings.
111	
112	    Mapping keys whose name matches the configured secret-name pattern
113	    have their value masked wholesale. String leaves pass through
114	    ``obfuscate_password`` so an embedded DSN credential nested
115	    arbitrarily deep is still scrubbed. Non-string scalars
116	    (``int`` / ``bool`` / ``None``) pass through unchanged.
117	    """
118	    if isinstance(value, dict):
119	        return {k: _MASK if isinstance(k, str) and is_secret_key(k) else _redact_value(v) for k, v in value.items()}
120	    if isinstance(value, list):
121	        return [_redact_value(item) for item in value]
122	    if isinstance(value, tuple):
123	        return tuple(_redact_value(item) for item in value)
124	    if isinstance(value, str):
125	        return obfuscate_password(value)
126	    return value

133	    :func:`configure_redaction`) are masked entirely; string leaves have
134	    any embedded connection-string password obfuscated; nested dicts /
135	    lists / tuples are walked recursively.
136	    """
137	    return _redact_value(arguments)  # type: ignore[no-any-return]
